classification.difficultyReason: Read signed Celsius temperatures from four supplied graduated scales.

content.prompt: Write down the reading for each thermometer shown below.

spec.description: Upright thermometer with scale to the right, labelled −40 through 100 every 10 degrees and minor ticks every 2 degrees. Liquid ends halfway between −20 and −10. Decorative casing gradients omitted.
spec.answerVisibility: Liquid level is a permanent given; numerical reading appears only in answers.

answer.worked: The liquid is halfway between $-20^\circ\mathrm C$ and $-10^\circ\mathrm C$, so the reading is $-15^\circ\mathrm C$.

spec.description: Upright Celsius thermometer, labelled −40 through 100 every 10 degrees, minor ticks every 2 degrees; liquid reaches −30. Decorative gradients omitted.
spec.answerVisibility: Liquid level is a permanent given; numerical reading appears only in answers.

answer.worked: The liquid reaches the $-30$ mark, so the reading is $-30^\circ\mathrm C$.

spec.description: Upright Celsius thermometer, labelled −40 through 100 every 10 degrees, minor ticks every 2 degrees; liquid reaches the first minor tick above −20. Decorative gradients omitted.
spec.answerVisibility: Liquid level is a permanent given; numerical reading appears only in answers.

answer.worked: Each small interval represents $2^\circ\mathrm C$. The liquid is one interval above $-20^\circ\mathrm C$, so the reading is $-18^\circ\mathrm C$.

spec.description: Upright Celsius thermometer, labelled −40 through 100 every 10 degrees, minor ticks every 2 degrees; liquid reaches −40. Decorative gradients omitted.
spec.answerVisibility: Liquid level is a permanent given; numerical reading appears only in answers.

answer.worked: The liquid reaches the $-40$ mark, so the reading is $-40^\circ\mathrm C$.
